title: Randy: The Contender Who Never Lets Go
body: Every league needs a franchise that shows up, wins more than it loses, and refuses to hand anyone anything, especially in a trade. That franchise is The fumblers, and the man behind it is Randy. In three completed seasons he has never finished below .500, never sniffed last place, and made the postseason every single year. He has also never lifted the Buckaroo Bowl, and the story of his career lives in the space between those facts.

Randy opened in 2023 with a 7-7 record, 1462.9 points, and the 3 seed, finishing third. That season also produced his career low, a 73.1-point dud against Kaushal in week 6. He made zero trades and five pickups, which tells you everything about his philosophy: draft your guys, love your guys, and keep your guys. In 2024 he climbed to 8-6 and the 2 seed, posted his best week ever (162.5 points in week 3, at Ramon's expense), and doubled his waiver activity to 10 pickups. He finished fourth, and his trade count stayed proudly at zero.

2025 was the breakthrough. The fumblers went 9-7, piled up a career-best 1792.1 points, earned the 2 seed again, and reached Buckaroo Bowl III, where Sonny's worst-to-first Ben Dover squad stood in the way. Randy finished second, the closest he has come to the crown. He also made the first trade of his career that year, a historic event for a manager who guards his roster like a Bears fan guards his last shred of hope in December. His 16 pickups showed a manager who had learned to work the wire, even if the trade button still makes him nervous.

The head-to-head ledger has some sharp edges. Randy owns Ramon at 7-4, making him one of the few people in the league who can claim Brucie's number, and he edges Kaushal 6-5. Mekhi has been a dead-even 6-6 dogfight. The trouble spots are Alan, who leads 5-8 and has turned Philliberto-versus-Randy into the league's most one-sided villain story, and Sonny, who holds a 5-3 edge. Randy is a perfect 1-0 against both newcomers, Jordan and Zoe, and you can bet the win over Zilgit got a Bears-over-Packers victory lap.

Which brings us to 2026, the toughest stretch of his career so far. The fumblers sit at 3-4 with 752.4 points, and the model gives them a 3% shot at the title. Randy has already made 14 pickups and another trade, so he is not standing still, but the results haven't followed yet. Three straight playoff trips and a 1-3 postseason record say this is a manager who knows how to get to the dance and is still looking for the right moves once he's there. Count him out at your own risk, though he'll be the first to complain about it.
